hook: The crime happened in another city. Can I still **file an FIR** here?
hook_q: What is a Zero FIR and how do I file an e-FIR?

slides.title: Yes. File at **any police station.**
slides.body: Information about a cognizable offence may be given to an officer in charge of a police station, irrespective of the area where the offence was committed. MHA calls this Zero FIR.

slides.title: Go in person, or **report electronically.**
slides.body: You can give the information orally or by electronic communication, without having to visit the police station.

timeline.text: You send the information by **electronic communication.**
You sign it. Only then is it **taken on record** by the officer in charge.

slides.title: Told orally? It's **read back to you.**
slides.body: Oral information must be written down by the officer or under their direction, read over to you, and signed by you.

slides.title: Your copy is **free.**
slides.body: A copy of the information as recorded must be given at once, free of cost, to the informant or the victim.

slides.title: How to report online **depends on your State.**
slides.body: Online options differ from State to State, so check your State police website. For cyber financial fraud, there's the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal and helpline 1930.

sources: PIB (MHA): E-FIR under BNSS, 11 Aug 2026; Key features of the new criminal laws, 20 Aug 2025; e-Zero FIR, 19 May 2025
MHA: Rajya Sabha Unstarred Q. 1182, 10 Dec 2025 (mha.gov.in)
caption:
Crime happened somewhere else? You can still go to the nearest police station. 👇

1️⃣ Information about a cognizable offence can be given to any police station, wherever the offence happened (Zero FIR)
2️⃣ You can give it orally or by electronic communication
3️⃣ Reported electronically? Sign it within 3 days so it is taken on record
4️⃣ You get a copy of the FIR free of cost
5️⃣ How to report online depends on your State's police. For cyber financial fraud, use the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal or call 1930

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Section 173; PIB/MHA
